title: Understanding the Trust Equation
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Trust equation: credibility, reliability and intimacy over self-orientation; first appeared in The Trusted Advisor (2000), co-written by Charles H. Green

title: Creating helpful, reliable, people-first content
supports: Opened with WebFetch. E-E-A-T; trust matters most; YMYL topics (health, financial stability, safety) get more weight; accurate bylines; fabricated creators and false credentials are deception

title: How consumers are choosing legal services (Tracker Survey 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (PDF read locally). 3,802 legal service users in England and Wales, surveyed 23 February to 13 April 2026: 42% shopped around; price (57%) and reputation (52%) most compared; 21% had used the provider before, 18% chose on a recommendation; 91% said a regulated provider was important; 74% found cost information easy to find, 56% found complaints and insurance information easy

title: Legal services market study
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Final report 15 December 2016 found competition for individual consumers and small businesses not working well and called for greater transparency

title: California Rule of Professional Conduct 7.1 and executive summary
supports: Opened with WebFetch (PDF read locally). Rule effective 1 November 2018: no false or misleading communications; truthful but misleading statements; guarantees of results; past results and testimonials can create unjustified expectations; unsubstantiated comparisons. The summary describes the ABA Model Rules framework (7.1 general, 7.2 advertising, 7.3 direct contact, 7.4 specialisation, 7.5 firm names). Used because americanbar.org blocks automated reading

title: SRA Code of Conduct for Solicitors, RELs and RFLs
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Version in effect from 11 April 2025: 8.7 best possible information on pricing; 8.8 publicity accurate and not misleading; 8.9 no unsolicited approaches to members of the public except current or former clients

title: SRA Transparency Rules
supports: Opened with WebFetch. In effect from 11 April 2025: price information for listed services (e.g. residential conveyancing, uncontested probate, employment tribunal claims, debt recovery); complaints procedure; SRA number and digital badge on the website

title: Model Code of Conduct for European Lawyers (2021)
publisher: Council of Bars and Law Societies of Europe (CCBE)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (PDF read locally). Adopted 8 October 2021; a model for member bars, not a uniform enforceable code; the separate CCBE Code of Conduct covers cross-border practice

title: ICAEW Code of Ethics
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Latest version came into force on 1 July 2026; links to the 2026 code

title: ICAEW Code of Ethics 2026 (PDF)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (PDF read locally). R115.2: marketing must not bring the profession into disrepute; be honest and truthful; no exaggerated claims; no disparaging references or unsubstantiated comparisons; consult the professional body if in doubt. R115.3: no promotion that amounts to harassment

title: The IESBA Code
publisher: International Ethics Standards Board for Accountants
supports: Opened with WebFetch. International code used in more than 130 jurisdictions; five fundamental principles including professional behaviour

title: 2026 Handbook of the International Code of Ethics for Professional Accountants
publisher: International Ethics Standards Board for Accountants
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Current edition published 24 September 2026; downloads need a sign-in

title: ACCA Rulebook
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Current edition 1 January 2026; includes the Code of Ethics and Conduct

title: Circular 230 information for tax professionals
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Rules for practice before the IRS covering attorneys, CPAs and enrolled agents; page reviewed 28 May 2026

title: Unfair Trade Practices Act (Model 880)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (PDF read locally). Spring 2024 printing of a model act that states may adopt or modify; bans misrepresenting policy benefits, terms or names and untrue, deceptive or misleading insurance advertising in any medium

title: Financial promotions and adverts
supports: Opened with WebFetch. All financial promotions must be clear, fair and not misleading in any media; insurance (home, motor, travel) is covered; links to ICOBS; updated 28 May 2024

title: FG24/1: Finalised guidance on financial promotions on social media
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Published 26 March 2024; promotions on social media must be fair, clear and not misleading and give a balanced picture; unauthorised people promoting without approval may commit a criminal offence; covers influencers

title: Consumer Duty
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The Duty sets high standards of protection for retail consumers across financial services and asks firms to put customers' needs first

title: Insurance Distribution Directive (IDD)
publisher: European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Directive (EU) 2016/97 regulates how insurance is designed and distributed; pre-contract information including the IPID; conduct and transparency rules; minimum harmonising, so member states may add rules

title: The Architects Code: Standards of professional conduct and practice
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The 2025 Code is in effect and replaced the 2017 version; Standard 1 is honesty and integrity

title: The Architects Code of Conduct and Practice 2025 (PDF)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (PDF read locally). Standard 1.2: architects promote their services responsibly and accurately

title: Who can use the title architect
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Only people on the Architects Register may use the title; anyone may provide architectural services; terms like architectural consultant are not protected; over 42,000 registered architects

title: FTC's Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Guides revised 2023; material connections must be disclosed clearly; a testimonial showing better-than-usual results needs the generally expected results; endorsements must reflect honest experience

title: Consumer Reviews and Testimonials Rule: Questions and Answers
supports: Opened with WebFetch. In effect from 21 October 2024; bans fake reviews and testimonials, incentives conditioned on positive or negative reviews, undisclosed insider reviews, company-controlled 'independent' review sites and review suppression

title: Fake engagement policy
supports: Opened with WebFetch. No incentives for reviews; no conflict-of-interest reviews from owners or staff; no discouraging negative reviews or selectively asking for positive ones; asking for genuine reviews without incentives is allowed

title: The CAP Code (UK Code of Non-broadcast Advertising and Direct and Promotional Marketing)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. ASA enforces the code; Section 3 covers misleading advertising, including substantiation, comparisons and testimonials

title: Influencers' guide to making clear that ads are ads
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Fourth edition dated 23 October 2026, made with the CMA; adds fake reviews and the DMCC Act

title: Unfair commercial practices (CMA207)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. CMA guidance on unfair commercial practices under the DMCC Act 2024, published 4 April 2025 and updated 18 November 2025; separate CMA guidance covers fake reviews (CMA208) and price transparency (CMA209)
